external_entities.name: other teams' backend
external_entities.description: Backend services operated by other teams that call the inference gateway.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
external_entities.notes: Keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

external_entities.name: calling team's user
external_entities.description: Users of the calling teams whose typed input may appear in raw prompts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed

external_entities.name: ML engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who publishes new model artifacts to the model registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket
external_entities.notes: The source says: "I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account."

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service on GKE that receives inference requests from calling backends and forwards them to the model server.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The server that runs the actual model on GPU nodes and loads model artifacts and customer features.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which the model server loads model artifacts at startup and to which ML engineers publish new artifacts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket."

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features including account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password and is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every request and response for debugging, including raw prompts that may contain users' typed input.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_stores.notes: Raw prompts sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: call inference
data_flows.description: A calling backend sends an inference request to the inference gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
data_flows.notes: Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and have never expired one.

data_flows.name: forward request
data_flows.description: The inference gateway forwards an inference request to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server
data_flows.notes: There is no authentication between the gateway and the model server.

data_flows.name: load artifacts
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup
data_flows.notes: The model server uses its own service account for access. The source says: "I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket."

data_flows.name: read features
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from the Redis feature store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the model server reads from a Redis feature store on the same network
data_flows.notes: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.
data_flows.data_description: customer features including account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: write log
data_flows.description: The inference gateway writes every request and response to the inference log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_flows.notes: The log contains raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.
data_flows.data_description: every request and response, including raw prompts

data_flows.name: publish artifacts
data_flows.description: An ML engineer publishes new model artifacts to the model registry bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account."

trust_boundaries.name: model network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the model server and Redis feature store are located; it is intended to be reachable only from the inference gateway.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway

assumptions.assumption: The inference gateway presents a web interface because it is described as a FastAPI service.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the gateway as a FastAPI service, and FastAPI is a web application framework.

assumptions.assumption: The customer features in the Redis feature store are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The store contains per-customer account age and spend bands, which are customer-specific information.
